title: NFIP Dwelling Form Flood Policies (Write Your Own) — Rise in the Full-Term Risk Premium for Contents-Limit Increases on Loan Transactions
content:
## Measuring the rise in the full-term risk premium — increase of the contents limit recorded for a loan transaction (NFIP Dwelling Form Flood Policies (Write Your Own))

For a pending increase of the contents limit recorded for a loan transaction on a tier that carries no ICC coverage, the rise in the full-term risk premium on which the charge is measured is set by the first line below that holds:

| Situation on the records | Rise in the full-term risk premium |
|---|---|
| The request carries no full-term risk premium from the rating engine | No rise |
| The building-limit increase recorded for the same loan closing — one that leaves the contents limit on the policy unchanged — has been billed, its endorsement charge being booked on the premium account | The request's full-term risk premium less that increase's full-term risk premium, because this request was rated on top of it |
| A re-rate credit from an applied Elevation Certificate was booked on the current term after the request was recorded | The request's full-term risk premium less the risk premium booked for the term at its start, because both figures stand on the rating basis the request was rated on |
| Otherwise | The request's full-term risk premium less the rated risk premium on the policy |

The risk premium booked for the term at its start is the risk premium charged for the current term at new business or at renewal. A re-rate credit counts here only when it is a credit on the risk premium line from an applied Elevation Certificate, posted on the current term after the date the request was recorded. The building-limit increase for the same loan closing is the coverage-increase request recording the same loan closing date that leaves the contents limit on the policy unchanged, the most recently recorded such request; it has been billed when an endorsement charge referencing it stands on the premium account.

*Hypothetical illustration.* A request carries a full-term risk premium of 1,500.00 dollars; the rated risk premium on the policy is 1,300.00 dollars and the risk premium booked for the term at its start was 1,400.00 dollars. If a building-limit increase for the same loan closing has been billed and carried a full-term risk premium of 1,450.00 dollars, the rise is 50.00 dollars (1,500.00 less 1,450.00). Without it, and with no re-rate credit after the request, the rise is 200.00 dollars (1,500.00 less 1,300.00); with such a re-rate credit, 100.00 dollars (1,500.00 less 1,400.00).
